summary.overview: Chaathan has strong agent instructions and a well-structured skill layer, but declared validation rules lack mechanical enforcement, one skill-pair carries a stale step-count discrepancy, and the observation window is too sparse to confirm learning-loop effectiveness.

dimensions.label: Task Understanding
dimensions.summary: AGENTS.md and six domain skills route agents to the correct package and state architecture constraints clearly; a step-count discrepancy between two skills slightly undermines guidance reliability.

dimensions.label: Controlled Execution
dimensions.summary: Makefile targets, WSL-specific commands, and a tools-check route provide a usable startup and operation surface; no doctor or state-reset command exists.

dimensions.label: Change Validation
dimensions.summary: Four validation layers (fmt, test, lint, build) and 33 test files are available, but no CI gate or affected-check routing connects them to individual changes.

dimensions.label: Reliable Delivery
dimensions.summary: No CI/CD pipeline, merge protection, or recovery command was detected; delivery acceptance and rollback remain unobserved from static evidence.

dimensions.label: Learning Capture
dimensions.summary: Six configured skills and a rich memory system are present, but the sparse 3-session window cannot validate routing, application, or later outcome improvement.

findings.title: Step-count discrepancy between chaathan-dev and chaathan-recon-workflows skills
findings.reason: chaathan-dev states '22 steps across 6 phases (Phases 0 to 5)' while chaathan-recon-workflows catalogs 21 steps (Steps 1-21) under the same 6 phases. An agent loading one skill receives a different workflow-length expectation than the other, risking missed or phantom steps during scan modification.
expectedOutput: Both chaathan-dev and chaathan-recon-workflows state the same canonical step count matching the code.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Audit pkg/scan/scan.go and pkg/wildcard_flow/flow.go step registry to count the actual registered steps. Update the incorrect skill document (.agents/skills/chaathan-dev/SKILL.md or .agents/skills/chaathan-recon-workflows/SKILL.md) to match the canonical count.

## Validation

- Count registered steps in the flow step registry
- Confirm both skills state the same step count
- Run go build -buildvcs=false -o chaathan . to confirm no code change was needed

findings.title: Declared validation baseline has no mechanical enforcement gate
findings.reason: AGENTS.md declares a four-command validation baseline (gofmt, go test, golangci-lint, go build), but no CI pipeline, pre-commit hook, or git hook enforces it. The four highest-churn files (17-21 commits in 30 days, up to 7,931 lines churn) can receive regressions that pass undetected when the manual validation loop is skipped.
expectedOutput: Every push and PR runs the four declared validation commands automatically and reports pass/fail status.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add a minimal CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) that runs the AGENTS.md validation baseline (gofmt -l ., go test ./..., golangci-lint run ./..., go build -buildvcs=false -o chaathan .) on push and pull_request events.

## Validation

- Push a trivial change and confirm the workflow triggers
- Confirm all four validation commands appear in the workflow log
- Verify the check status appears on the PR

findings.title: Architecture rules duplicated across AGENTS.md and chaathan-architecture-principles skill
findings.reason: The seven core architecture rules appear in both AGENTS.md (which declares itself canonical) and .agents/skills/chaathan-architecture-principles/SKILL.md (which restates them in expanded form). When one copy is updated without the other, agents loading both surfaces receive conflicting guidance about ownership boundaries and extension patterns.
expectedOutput: One canonical copy of the architecture rules with the skill adding non-overlapping detail and an explicit reference.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Designate AGENTS.md as the single canonical source for architecture rules. In .agents/skills/chaathan-architecture-principles/SKILL.md, replace the restated rules with a reference to AGENTS.md and keep only the expanded topology, anti-patterns, and extension guidance that adds value beyond the root file.

## Validation

- Confirm the architecture rules appear verbatim in only one file
- Confirm the skill references AGENTS.md for the canonical rule text
- Trigger both surfaces and verify no contradictory rule statements remain

findings.title: No affected-package test route documented for focused validation
findings.reason: The Makefile test target and AGENTS.md validation baseline run the full suite (go test ./...) without a documented route for scoping tests to changed packages. With 33 test files across 20+ packages, agents modifying a single package receive no guided fast-feedback path, increasing validation time as the project grows.
expectedOutput: Agents can run package-scoped tests as a fast first-pass check, with the full suite as the final gate.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add a test-focused Makefile target (e.g., test-pkg PKG=./pkg/wildcard_flow/...) that runs go test -race on the specified package. Document it in the AGENTS.md validation baseline as the recommended first-pass check before the full suite.

## Validation

- Run make test-pkg PKG=./pkg/wildcard_flow/... and confirm only that package's tests execute
- Confirm the full make test still passes
- Verify AGENTS.md documents both focused and full validation routes
